Just wanted to announce quadratic-forms-lean as an AI-authored Lean 4 library on quadratic forms over number fields, written with Claude Code (mostly Claude Opus 5.5) over about a week. Its first release v0.1.0 has these main results:

- Siegel's theorem for totally positive definite quadratic lattices representing numbers over totally real fields (every rank and every genus)
- τ(SO(Q))=2\tau(\mathrm{SO}(Q)) = 2τ(SO(Q))=2 and the mass formula over totally real fields
- Hasse–Minkowski over number fields (isotropy, representation, isometry)
- Hilbert reciprocity over number fields, by a local proof through the Weil index (Tau Ceti has a proof through class field theory)

I'd like to contribute what's useful here to Tau Ceti and Mathlib, and I'd welcome suggestions on which pieces would be most valuable and how best to bring them over.

Thanks!
-Jon

P.S. Proofs are kernel-checked with standard axioms only. The headline statements are in Challenge.lean (its only sorrys are the deliberate statement-only ones), and lake comparator checks them against the proofs. formalization.yaml records the sources, the scope and the cost (roughly $1.2–1.8k at list prices, on a flat-rate plan). I've reviewed the headline statements and the definitions they use; the rest of the library hasn't had human review, so reports of mis-formalizations are welcome.

Just noting that there is a firm rule that participants on the zulip must not use LLMs to write their text. (Clearly labelled /spoiler sections are fine.) This holds just as much in the "AI and Lean" folder, or the AI authored projects channel. Doing so may result in messages being deleted and accounts suspended.

:robot: Here's what the AIs say about the overlaps between this project and Tau Ceti

Already done in Tau Ceti: Hilbert reciprocity over arbitrary number fields; local classification by dimension, discriminant and Hasse invariant, including dyadic fields; Witt’s theorems in characteristic ≠2; Jordan splittings over ℤₚ; reduction theory, finiteness of positive definite lattice classes over ℤ, and integral genera.

We have roadmaps for the following, so it would be great to start PRing these parts to Tau Ceti: Hasse–Minkowski for isotropy, representation and isometry over number fields is covered by GlobalQuadraticForms, although only conditional induction steps are implemented. Local densities over ℤₚ are covered by IntegralLattices, Layer 7. Dirichlet’s imaginary-quadratic class-number formula is covered by ImaginaryQuadraticClassNumber, H2.2, and Legendre’s three-square theorem by ClassicalArithmeticCompletion, §4.81.

Open roadmap PRs (help reviewing these would be appreciated): Siegel’s genus-average representation formula falls within the Siegel–Weil programme of #1063, with a more restricted rank-one identity also in #851. Orthogonal Tamagawa numbers and lattice mass formulas are covered by #851 and #1222. Weil indices and their product formula are covered by #1063; strong approximation for Spin and Eichler’s theorem by #1222. These are topic-level matches; individual proposals have rank, maximality and base-field restrictions.

Someone will need to write roadmaps for: Witt’s extension, cancellation and decomposition theorems in characteristic two. That theory is explicitly excluded from the approved QuadraticFormInvariants scope, and I found no open proposal covering it.
I converted the conversation that produced the report above into a SKILL.md. Seems plausibly useful elsewhere.
